<div id="guidelines-for-using-ai-tools" class="section">

<span id="generative-ai"></span><span id="ai-tools"></span>

# Guidelines for using AI tools<a href="#guidelines-for-using-ai-tools" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

The person submitting an issue or PR is responsible for its content,
regardless of whether AI tools were used in its creation. Generative AI
tools can produce output quickly, but discretion, good judgment, and
critical thinking are the foundation of all good contributions. We value
good code, concise accurate documentation, and well scoped PRs without
unneeded code churn.

<div id="considerations-for-success" class="section">

## Considerations for success<a href="#considerations-for-success" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Authors must review the work done by AI tooling in detail to ensure it
actually makes sense before proposing it as a PR or filing it as an
issue.

We expect PR authors and those filing issues to be able to explain their
proposed changes in their own words.

Disclosure of the use of AI tools in the PR description is appreciated,
while not required. Be prepared to explain how the tool was used and
what changes it made.

Whether you are using AI tools or not, keep the following principles in
mind for the quality of your contribution:

- Consider whether the change is necessary

- Make minimal, focused changes

- Follow existing coding style and patterns

- Write tests that exercise the change

- Keep backwards compatibility with prior releases in mind. Existing
  tests may be ensuring specific API behaviors are maintained.

Pay close attention to AI generated recommendations for testing changes.
Provide input about Python’s testing principles when guiding an AI
model. Always review the output before opening a pull request or issue,
including proposed PR or issue titles and descriptions.

</div>

<div id="acceptable-uses" class="section">

## Acceptable uses<a href="#acceptable-uses" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Some of the acceptable uses of generative AI include:

- Assistance with writing comments, especially in a non-native language

- Gaining understanding of existing code

- Supplementing contributor knowledge for code, tests, and documentation

</div>

<div id="unacceptable-uses" class="section">

## Unacceptable uses<a href="#unacceptable-uses" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Maintainers may close issues and PRs that are not useful or productive,
without explanation, regardless of whether AI tools were used or not.

If a contributor repeatedly opens unproductive issues or PRs, they may
be blocked from contributing to the project because it is disruptive and
disrespectful of the maintainers time.

It is not acceptable to alter or bypass existing tests, or remove
desired functionality, in order to make a failing test pass. Such
changes are not a real fix.

</div>

<div id="how-these-guidelines-are-applied" class="section">

## How these guidelines are applied<a href="#how-these-guidelines-are-applied" class="headerlink"
title="Link to this heading">¶</a>

Using AI tools is not a reason on its own for an issue or PR to be
labeled or closed. When a maintainer thinks an issue or PR does not
follow these guidelines, they may apply one of the following labels. A
bot then posts a comment that links to this page.

- <a href="https://github.com/python/cpython/labels/AI-needs-explanation"
  class="extlink-gh-label reference external">AI-needs-explanation</a>:
  the issue or PR stays open. Reply in your own words: explain what the
  change does or what the issue is about, and describe how you checked
  that it is correct.

- <a href="https://github.com/python/cpython/labels/AI-guidelines-not-met"
  class="extlink-gh-label reference external">AI-guidelines-not-met</a>:
  the issue or PR is closed. If you think we misunderstood your
  contribution, reply on the issue or PR. You are welcome to explain
  your approach or ask questions about these guidelines.

</div>

</div>
